_note: Steps that make a game model from a ComfyUI run (ASSET_PIPELINE.md 'Image to model'): the record art-manifest/comfy/<id>.json lists them and tools/blender/make.mjs build <id> does them in order on the run's detailed model (art-src/comfy/<id>/<run.file>), writing the record's game file beside it. Positions are shares (0 to 1) of the model's box in its game placement (the record's frame: z up, facing +y). Types: int, number, bool, enum (values), vec (a list of len numbers), boxes (lists of six numbers x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1), map (an object of fields), list (min to max objects of fields), file (a .glb file name beside the run's model), picture (a .png file name beside it), concept (a .png under art-src/concepts/). A new kind is an entry here plus its arguments in make.mjs (STEP_ARGS).

bend.what: Turn a part of the detailed model about a joint, paint and maps untouched (the bone hound's head raised 20 degrees at the neck, so its open jaw faces the game camera). Each corner turns by angle x its weight: 0 behind blend[0], 1 past blend[1] (along y), only above `above` (z). Before finish.

parts.what: Close-up parts fitted onto the detailed body, each keeping its own paint: a part too small for Pixal3D to read in the whole picture (a face, the skull on a shoulder plate) drawn large on its own and made into its own model (`file`, a model-gen run beside the run's model). Pixal3D's white fill (no subject there: a neck under a head) cut off, turned so the side its picture saw faces `facing` (the subject's own left and right), sized to `box` times `scale`, turned `tilt` degrees about its middle (a part drawn in another pose than the body wears it: a shoulder plate drawn from outside the arm lies over the shoulder at tilt 40, scale 1.3), and set at the depth the body has there. picture (a front part): its close-up under art-src/concepts/, which sizes and places it where it matches the record's picture best, when one place stands out (else the box). join: piece (the default): the body's own surface inside and just over the part goes, except where that would open a hole; surface (a head in its hood): the body keeps its hood and the part's face shows where the concept's front label (the materials step's) marks skin, the body's surface there pushed back behind it (what still stands in front is cut) and the part's own brim left to the body's. box: [x0, z0, x1, z1], where the part is on the body's picture as shares of the detailed model's own box (x the picture's left to right, z bottom to top). mirror: a copy on the other side (one shoulder plate made, both worn). rigid: armour that moves as one piece (a shoulder plate, a gorget): the rig gives all of it the same bone weights. Before finish.

finish.what: The game version of the detailed model: a solid rebuild (cells voxels across; method meshopt: none, the detailed surface itself cut down by meshoptimizer, which keeps faces, folds and thin cloth crisp on a clean model such as a hero), cut to `triangles` (the model's budget), fresh UVs in a few large charts packed by xatlas, and the detailed model's paint, roughness, metal and normals baked onto them at `texture` px. metal: none (stone, bone, wood, cloth, flesh), mixed (decided per material), all (by colour), keep (as Pixal made it); metalRegions {boxes, rough} where the metal is when Pixal marks the whole model metal. keep {boxes, share}: parts the cut takes last, so they hold that share of the triangles (a jaw and its fangs). hard: sharp edges kept (smooth by `angle` degrees). A body with close-up parts (a parts step): each part's paint moved, partScale (default 1.5) times the texture size on its charts, partTris (default 0.3; 0 lets the cut decide) of the triangles.

materials.what: What each part of the finished model is made of, and its shine: a label picture per view (`labels`: a .png beside the run's model, the same framing as the picture the model was made from, each pixel's red 1 metal, 2 leather, 3 cloth, 4 skin, 5 hair, 6 bone, 7 wood, 8 stone, 9 gem, 0 unknown) gives every texel its camera sees a material, the rest from the nearest seen texels of like colour, then by matching colours. Each material gets its own roughness and metal, varied by the paint's light and dark; metal gets worn bright edges and dark crevices (`wear`, 0 none to 2), and the occlusion is lightened to `occlusion` of its depth (Pixal3D bakes it deep: dull, flat paint). After finish, before place.

place.what: Move the model into its game placement (the record's frame, found by make.mjs fit). After finish, before rig.

grime.what: Dirt painted into the colour (and roughness) of a model that came out too clean: film everywhere, crevice grime, stains, mud from the feet, dust on top, old-bone yellowing (age), all scaled by amount. After place (it needs the game's up).

rig.what: A skeleton built from the placed model's shape, the body skinned by geodesic voxel binding. body: quad (four legs: Root, Hip, Spine1-2, Chest, Neck1-2, Head, Tail_A-D, FL/FR_Upper/Lower/Paw, HL/HR_Thigh/Shin/Meta/Paw; legTop 0.8 when hanging cloth meets the legs low), legs (any number of legs around one body, a spider's eight: Root, Hip, Abdomen, Head, <side><n>_Upper/Lower/Foot), biped (the heroes' skeleton on a body in a T or A pose, the body turned to face +X like every hero body; refused when its feet then point backwards). No clips: they are Blender jobs (a motion on tools/blender/recipes/<id>.json; a biped's, a retarget from hero_gravecaller). Last.
